title: Kinfolk learning Gifts
summary: What a Gift costs a Kinfolk.

claims.text: A Kinfolk earns a Gift through bargaining with Garou or spirits, practice, gifts, chiminage and sometimes a quest, and only then spends experience on it.
A Gift of the Kin’s own breed or tribe costs 15 points, with 5 more if it lies outside them and 5 more if a Garou teaches it instead of a spirit.
Kin seldom get Gifts from outside their own breed or tribe, since breeds and tribes guard their Gifts closely; special need or a whole sept’s welfare can make an exception.

title: Rite of Homestead Dedication
summary: A level two Kinfolk rite for a new home.

claims.text: When Kinfolk gain a new home, this rite gives the building and its land to Gaia’s service, a weaker cousin of the Rite of Caern Building.
It can be repeated at each stage, from buying the plot and breaking ground to the family’s first night inside.
Most versions walk a circle around the land and the house while calling on Gaia, the tribal totem and any spirits already tied to the place.

title: Spirit Chasing
summary: A hedge magic Way of bonding with an animal or plant.

claims.text: A spirit chaser forms a bond with one kind of plant or animal, believing every living thing has a spirit, and learns by watching it.
Unlike Gift teaching, no bargain is struck: the chaser observes the spirit, questions and copies it, then pleads in a private ritual for it to appear, which can take a long time.

title: Kin-Fetches and breaking the bond
summary: How Garou release a fetch from a Kin who never Changes.

claims.text: Once it seems plain that a bonded Kin will never undergo the First Change, the werewolf relatives usually use a form of the Rite of Spirit Awakening to wipe the fetch brand and free the Kin-Fetch for other cubs.
Callow Kin who went through the Baptism of Fire must be handled more quietly, usually while drugged.

Loosely organised Fera such as most Bastet rely on the practice even more, and the more nomadic a breed, the more it may lean on its own Baptism of Fire; Corax, for one, may bind a Kin-Fetch very early.
The Locksmiths began in the late 1990s, founded by a Glass Walker called only Strangelove, as a network for Glass Walker Kinfolk.
Garou and Kin worldwide use it to stay in touch and follow Pentex and other Wyrm-tainted firms, and it now runs a site on fracking and its natural and supernatural dangers.
Its first projects were two large databases, the first a list of every known tainted product.
